thread:
Owen: FYI - we started seeing p99 spikes on hydra-3 for long inputs after the tokenizer normalization change rolled yesterday evening. Two paying customers hit 30s+ latencies and a couple of timeouts. attaching quick traces in-thread.
Priya: ack. rough numbers? is this hosted only or hitting Dedicated too?
Owen: Hosted + Dedicated; seems most pronounced on requests with >12k tokens. Quick before/after from staging run:
  - hydra-3 v1.3 (pre-change): p50 0.18s, p95 1.2s, p99 2.1s
  - hydra-3 v1.4 (post-normalizer): p50 0.19s, p95 2.8s, p99 18.9s
  tokenization_time_ms increased ~10x for long sequences.
Alex: do we have a repro curl we can share to hit the same path? want to try from cluster to rule out network.
Owen: repro below (use long prompt repeat). this triggers normalization codepath.
```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"model":"hydra-3","input":"'$(printf 'hello %.0s' {1..20000})'"}'
```
Leah: saw the infra alert from deploy-bot around 1769900000 indicating tokenizer package pushed to prod. infra-bot, can you link the release? :eyes:
infra-bot: Release 2026-03-12T22:04Z pushed tokenizer-normalizer v1.4 -> hydra-3. CI perf buckle tests passed but long-seq synthetic tests were limited to 8k.
support-bot: Customer ticket #C-23984 created by AcmeCorp: "/generate for long docs times out on hydra-3". Support flagged as P1.
Priya: hypothesis: normalizer increases splitting for multi-byte sequences (CJK + emojis) causing token count blowup + more KV cache misses -> extra decode iterations. Owen, can you paste an example token log showing before/after token counts?
Owen: pasted snippets:
```
# pre-normalizer
orig_len=10240 tok_count=10250 tokenize_ms=45 kv_miss=false
# post-normalizer
orig_len=10240 tok_count=15872 tokenize_ms=510 kv_miss=true
```
Alex: that explains it. bump in tokens => cost and tail latency. quick mitigations:
  1) add temporary routing policy: requests with header `x-input-length>12000` -> hydra-2 or hydra-3-legacy tokenzier
  2) disable normalizer for inputs > 8k in tokenizer at runtime and hot-reload
  3) scale up hydra-3 pools for hosted (short-term)
Leah: ops can scale hosted pools, but Dedicated customers might still hit timeouts if their reserved nodes are saturated.
Priya: also check billing/throttles; some retries due to 504s could amplify tail. any evidence of retries in logs?
Owen: yes, a few clients retried automatically; we saw retry loop from SDK v0.9 with exponential backoff disabled by default in earlier versions; that amplified p99 for a small subset.
Leah: immediate plan: (A) hot-disable normalizer for long inputs (Leah + Alex), (B) push routing policy -> hydra-2 for inputs >12k (Priya will coordinate with product), (C) customer comms draft (Owen) and ticket updates. timeline target: 2h for hotfix, 4h for routing policy.
Alex: I'll prepare the rollback PR that toggles normalizer flag and a runtime config. include guard to only affect hosted until we validate dedicated behavior.
Priya: assign escalation owner to keep customers updated. Owen pls post brief note with ETA in ticket and link here.
Owen: doing now. draft to customers: "we've identified a tokenizer normalization regression impacting very long inputs on hydra-3. We're rolling a hotfix to disable the normalization for long inputs and will provide a routing fallback. ETA ~2h. Apologies for the disruption." :handshake:
support-bot: Noted. Ticket #C-23984 updated and customers notified.
Leah: after hotfix, let's run an A/B with sample long inputs and monitor p95/p99 for 1 hour before full re-enable. also add unit test for sequences up to 32k for future releases.
Owen: agreed. I'll attach perf harness link and results once done.
Alex: one more: add a temporary telemetry metric `tokenizer.normalizer.enabled_for_length` and alert if p99>5s for >1% of long requests.
Priya: good. Thanks team. keep thread updated.
Owen: will update in ~30m with hotfix status.
